evals.name: routing-triggers
evals.prompt: go through the open GitHub issues and fix the bugs
evals.expected_output: issues-fix loads, lists the open bug issues, verifies each still reproduces against the code, groups them by subsystem, and fixes the approved groups one at a time.

evals.name: routing-excludes-task-run
evals.expected_output: One known issue handed over directly is task-run's job; issues-fix must not load, because there is no backlog to triage or group.

evals.name: routing-triggers-file-backlog
evals.prompt: work through the list in issues.md and fix everything in it
evals.expected_output: issues-fix loads, reads issues.md as the backlog, verifies each unticked item is real and not already done, groups them, and fixes the approved groups one at a time — ticking each item as its fix merges. It must not require gh or a GitHub remote to do it.

evals.name: groups-run-one-at-a-time-in-one-tree
evals.expected_output: Approved groups are fixed strictly serially, each on its own feature branch merged into the base before the next starts. Two fixes running in one working tree collide on that base ref, so parallelising the fix phase is not an optimisation available to a plain run, however independent the groups look. The only thing that moves that boundary is an explicit --cmux, which puts each group in its own detached worktree — a tree that takes base without claiming the ref — and runs two of them at the same time only where the touches are disjoint, none of them deep and none resting on a low-confidence verdict; the rest still run one at a time, each in a tree of its own. Without the flag, none of that happens and the loop is serial in the one working tree.

evals.name: verification-rejects-items-already-done
evals.expected_output: Each candidate is read against the actual code by a read-only verifier before anything is fixed, and an item already implemented, no longer applicable, or resting on a false premise is dropped and named with its reason in the report — not handed to a fixer that will produce an empty diff.

evals.name: both-halves-are-workflows-in-the-main-thread
evals.expected_output: Each approved group is the real run-task-implement Workflow followed by the real /r:task-review Workflow, both driven from the caller's own main thread by scriptPath. Neither half is imitated in prose, and neither is nested inside a subagent where its fan-out would collapse.

evals.name: cmux-only-parallelises-what-it-can-prove-is-disjoint
evals.expected_output: Groups run at the same time only when the union of their members' touches is disjoint, and a group that is deep, or that holds any low-confidence verdict, is held out and fixed alone — with the reason said out loud rather than left to inference. touches is a verifier's estimate, not a written file list, which is why the margin is wider here than in a plan-run wave. Being held out costs a group its wave-mates, never its workspace: every group is fixed in a full interactive claude session in its own detached worktree and cmux workspace, a wave of one included, and nothing is fixed in the orchestrator's own tree. A solo group is landed before the next worktree is cut. At most three are live at once, and each one's workspace and worktree come down the moment it reports ok, freeing the slot for the next. A group that failed or stalled is left standing and named. Merging and issue-closing happen only from the primary tree, after the wave.

evals.name: only-restricts-the-run-to-exactly-those-items
evals.expected_output: Discovery is skipped entirely: exactly those two items are taken, located by their verbatim text, and nothing else in issues.md is verified, grouped or fixed. A ref that resolves to no item stops the run rather than quietly fixing the remainder — a session handed a group it cannot find must not report having fixed part of it.
